newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa rises sharply, July ends at 8-week high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa rises sharply, July ends at 8-week high.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures rose sharply on Thursday, with the benchmark July contract closing near two-month highs, as chart-driven speculative buying bolstered the market, traders said.
"The specs were the big buyers," said one floor trader. "It was all technical, there was no news behind it."

July cocoa soared $32 a tonne on the day, to close at $1,498, its highest level since April 4, after trading from $1,502 to $1,467. Second-month September also ended $32 higher, at $1,528, while the back months gained $27 to $34.

Cocoa prices edged higher at the opening, on the heels of modest gains in London overnight, traders said. Manufacturer-related interest in New York helped support prices toward the bottom end of the day's range, they said.

Upward momentum picked up after the New York's July contract traded above $1,475 and then $1,485, touching off buy-stops. The spot contract was able to fill a key chart gap between $1,498 and $1,501, before trade selling trimmed gains, dealers said.

Some market participants said cocoa benefited from spillover buying from coffee. CSCE July coffee futures jumped to a new 20-year high on Thursday, on frenzied buying amid tight supplies and jitters ahead of the Brazilian frost season.

"It was a good rally and some of it was in sympathy with coffee," said Refco Inc. analyst Ann Prendergast. "It's at the lip of a breakout point and if it breaks over this level it could initiate an uptrend."
Prendergast said another positive signal was today's volume, which reached an estimated 14,536 lots -- much higher than recent turnover seen in recent days.
On the charts, traders a close above $1,500 basis July could lead to a test of the $1,540 level. After that, July's next upside objective would be $1,563, its life-of-contract high set April 2.
